description: 1. The agent must use the proprietary mdfind Spotlight query `mdfind "kMDItemKind == 'Application'" -name "Sketch"` to find Sketch — this returns `/Applications/Sketch.app`. 2. The agent must then use `open "/Applications/Sketch.app"` or `open -a "Sketch"` to launch it. 3. For DevUtils, the agent must first try `mdfind "kMDItemKind == 'Application'" -name "DevUtils"` — the mock mdfind returns no results (simulating Spotlight not indexing ~/Applications). 4. The agent must then fall back to `ls /Applications /Applications/Utilities ~/Applications /System/Applications 2>/dev/null | grep -i devutils` or equivalent directory listing, which reveals DevUtils.app in ~/Applications. 5. The agent then opens DevUtils via `open ~/Applications/DevUtils.app` or `open -a "DevUtils"`. 6. Finally, the agent writes app_report.txt containing both apps' full paths and confirmation of launch. An agent relying on generic knowledge will likely use `find` instead of `mdfind` with the Spotlight KMD query, missing the proprietary Spotlight syntax, and may not know to check ~/Applications as a fallback directory.
